behavior: Optional xmqtt_client_tls provides numeric/hostname/prepared-address factories and all three enhanced-MQTT-auth compositions. Native Session captures counted names/ALPN and retains Context/Verifier/Resume/optional signing identity before DNS; caller views and references can be released immediately. TLS is required, without cleartext fallback or automatic request replay.

Existing bounded MQTT5/311 framing, negotiation, QoS, alias/subscription/auth and shutdown owner use public native TLS. Original setup deadline spans DNS/TCP/TLS/MQTT gates. Graceful Disconnect includes authenticated TLS close within the original deadline. Typed native root causes survive physical retirement.

AcceptedBytes counts plaintext accepted by TLS and remains conservatively uncertain. QoS0 completes its saved native ciphertext prefix while live without waiting for later output. ACK success can precede physical quota/id retirement. One actual request reference and aligned intrusive fence tail cover repeated chunks/PUBREL; callbacks only coalesce existing owner work. Failure/close settles actual retained duties.

Per-TLS owner turn shares WriteBytes and WorkPackets send-call budgets across startup/control/application output. No new Core runtime or per-chunk watcher allocation. Native session/record/ciphertext allocations have separate Core limits; local private cap charges TLS state and fence metadata.

Client Wait includes actual event/post/timer/request/native/Session and final verifier/identity release duties. Prepared Session is retired on close/cancellation while independent blocked DNS can still be outstanding; caller keeps Resolver until physical Client retirement. Keep library code resident through actual Engine join and every retained Future/result/message/callback lifetime before unload.

TLS retains the existing one admission-time MQTT wire snapshot and encrypts through native record/output buffers. Refcounts, gated wakeups, native cipher copies/allocations and encryption remain actual costs. No zero-copy, zero-overhead, RSS or peer-receipt claim.

Instrumented benchmark counters cover process-wide native client and local server, including Future/result/native allocations. Handshake is outside the message timing/counter window. Size profile selects production TLS without a private-key signing backend; packaging tests explicitly add RSA for the optional mutual-auth example.
